heading: EXT. DRY CREEK BED BENEATH A TRESTLE BRIDGE - DAWN

units.text: EXT. DRY CREEK BED BENEATH A TRESTLE BRIDGE - DAWN
A ribbon of cracked clay winds between two banks of sage.
Above, the old trestle spans the gap like the ribs of a long-dead animal, and the first light slides along its timbers in gold and rust.
A STRANGER (40s, long coat the color of dried blood, hat low, a face the weather has been arguing with for years) walks his horse down the bank in no particular hurry.
The animal's hooves crunch on the clay.
He halts at the creek's center and swings down, loosens the cinch, and lets the horse stand, ears flicking at the early flies.
Across the creek, on the opposite bank, sits a YOUNG WOMAN (20s, a man's shirt rolled at the sleeves, hair cut short with a knife, a shotgun resting across her knees) on a stump.
She has been sitting there all night.
A cold fire, a tin cup, a bedroll folded precisely, and a boot print the size of a dinner plate in the dirt beside her.
She does not raise the shotgun.
She does not lower her eyes.
Morning.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: That's debatable.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: I'm looking for a man named Cullen Pike.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Never heard of him.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: He wears a green scarf. Even in summer. Rides a gray with a split ear.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: The Young Woman shifts the shotgun a little.
A pale hawk circles over the bridge, riding the first warm air, and the Stranger watches it for a moment instead of her.
What do you want with him?
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: He's got something of mine.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Everybody's got something of somebody's.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: She stands.
The stump creaks.

She crosses the clay with the shotgun in the crook of her arm, stopping ten paces from him, and he, in answer, takes his hand away from the horse's flank and lets it hang loose and open beside his coat.
What's your name, mister?
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: The Stranger's eyes go to the bridge.
To the hawk.
To her.
Jedediah.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: That's a church name.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: My mother had hopes.
units.name: JEDEDIAH

units.text: She laughs, one short breath, and it startles her more than it does him.
The shotgun dips an inch.
He notices.
He says nothing about it.
I'm Odalys. Cullen was my father.
units.name: YOUNG WOMAN

units.text: Was.
units.name: JEDEDIAH

units.text: He's under the second pier. Since Tuesday.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Jedediah turns his head slowly and looks up the creek bed toward the trestle, its shadow now laid across the clay in long black bars.
At the foot of the second pier, a mound of fresh-turned earth, a plank driven in at its head.
He takes off his hat.
Holds it against his chest.
A breeze comes up and the sage whispers and the hawk screams once and swings away.
Who put him there?
units.name: JEDEDIAH

units.text: I did.
units.name: ODALYS

units.text: Who killed him?
units.name: JEDEDIAH

units.text: Odalys raises the shotgun, finally, and levels it at his belt buckle.
Her hands do not shake.
The man who sent you.
units.name: ODALYS
